newsitem.title: SPAIN: Ukraine signs security charter with NATO.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine signs security charter with NATO.

text.p: Ukraine signed a special charter with NATO on Wednesday that will give the former Soviet republic the right to call for "consultations" with NATO if it feels externally threatened.
Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma signed the pact, the "Charter on a Distinctive Partnership between NATO and Ukraine", at the start of the second day of a two-day meeting of NATO leaders in Madrid.

Ukraine is not seeking to join NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organisation), which on Tuesday extended an invitation of membership to three former Warsaw Pact nations. But the pact marked the culmination of long negotiations on how to strengthen ties without arousing Russian ire.

The charter sets up a series of mechanisms for contacts between NATO and Ukraine. There will be an exchange of military missions, with NATO establishing an office in Kiev, while meetings at ambassadorial level will be held once a month.

A NATO-Ukraine Commission will meet twice a year and provide the vehicle for "consultations" at times of regional crisis. Ukraine became the world's third largest nuclear power after the Soviet Union split up in 1991, but has since removed all nuclear warheads from its SS-19 and SS-24 long-range missiles.

Ukraine, which was ruled from Moscow for more than three centuries, was the first member of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) grouping former Soviet republics to join NATO's Partnership for Peace Programme.
